section_title: Definitions
statutory_summary: Establishes foundational definitions and general legal concepts for the entire Code, including claim, debt, default, corporate debtor, creditor, financial service provider, security interest, and service provider.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether an entity, obligation, transaction, or claim meets the general statutory definitions required to invoke or apply the provisions of the Code.

applicant_eligibility: Applies across all entities, creditors, debtors, and service providers governed by the Code.
Explicitly excludes financial service providers from the definition of a corporate person under Section 3(7).
mandatory_prerequisites: Definitions apply throughout the Code unless the context otherwise requires.
statutory_bars: Entities acting as financial service providers are excluded from the scope of corporate person/corporate debtor.
Security interest explicitly excludes performance guarantees and security interests created merely by operation of law.
saving_exceptions: Expressions used but not defined in the Code adopt meanings assigned under the Indian Contract Act 1872, Companies Act 2013, SEBI Act 1992, LLP Act 2008, and other specified Acts under Section 3(37).

section_title: Application of this Part
statutory_summary: Establishes the minimum default threshold required to initiate corporate insolvency, liquidation, or pre-packaged insolvency processes under Part II of the Code.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the amount of default committed by the corporate debtor meets or exceeds the statutory minimum threshold of one crore rupees (or the amount notified by the Central Government).

applicant_eligibility: Applies to matters relating to the insolvency and liquidation of corporate debtors under Part II.
Applies to corporate debtors eligible for pre-packaged insolvency resolution process under Chapter III-A.
mandatory_prerequisites: Existence of a default committed by a corporate debtor that meets or exceeds the statutory monetary threshold.
statutory_bars: Default amount is below the statutory threshold of one crore rupees (or below the threshold notified by the Central Government).
saving_exceptions: Central Government notification mechanism specifying a minimum default value of higher value up to one crore rupees for Part II matters.
Central Government notification mechanism specifying a distinct minimum default value of higher value up to one crore rupees for Chapter III-A pre-packaged insolvency matters.

section_title: Definitions
statutory_summary: Provides statutory definitions for key legal terms and expressions used throughout Part II of the Code, including Adjudicating Authority, financial debt, operational debt, corporate applicant, related party, avoidance transaction, and resolution plan.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether a person, debt, transaction, cost, or process satisfies the specific statutory definitions and criteria prescribed for the purpose of Part II proceedings.

applicant_eligibility: Specifies qualifying criteria for corporate applicants (corporate debtor, authorized member/partner, individual managing operations, or controller of financial affairs).
Defines financial creditors (persons owed financial debt) and operational creditors (persons owed operational debt).
Defines resolution applicants who submit resolution plans pursuant to invitations under Section 25(2)(h) or Section 54K.
mandatory_prerequisites: Terms must be construed in accordance with their specific statutory definitions for all proceedings under Part II unless the context otherwise requires.
statutory_bars: Excludes claims that do not fall within the scope of financial debt (disbursed against consideration for time value of money) or operational debt (goods, services, employment, or government dues).
Restricts related parties of the corporate debtor or individual from exercising voting rights in the committee of creditors under Part II provisions.
saving_exceptions: Real estate project allottees are explicitly deemed to have amounts with the commercial effect of a borrowing under Section 5(8)(f).

Financial entities regulated by financial sector regulators are exempted from certain related party disqualifications if related solely due to debt-to-equity conversion prior to the insolvency commencement date.

section_title: Persons who may initiate corporate insolvency resolution process
statutory_summary: Establishes locus standi for initiating the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP), granting standing exclusively to financial creditors, operational creditors, and the corporate debtor itself upon the occurrence of a default.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the applicant qualifies as a financial creditor, operational creditor, or corporate applicant, and whether a default has been committed by the corporate debtor.

applicant_eligibility: Financial creditor (individually or jointly with other financial creditors)
Operational creditor
Corporate debtor itself (through a corporate applicant)
mandatory_prerequisites: Occurrence of a default by the corporate debtor as defined under Section 3(12)
Compliance with the initiation procedure specified under Section 7, Section 9, or Section 10
statutory_bars: Applicant does not fall into one of the three enumerated statutory categories
No default has occurred
Applicant is barred under Section 11

section_title: Initiation of corporate insolvency resolution process by financial creditor
statutory_summary: Empowers financial creditors, either individually or jointly, to initiate the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) against a corporate debtor upon default, establishing specific numerical thresholds for class creditors and real estate allottees.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether a financial default has occurred, whether the applicant meets statutory class/quorum thresholds where applicable, whether the application is complete, and whether any disciplinary proceeding is pending against the proposed interim resolution professional.

applicant_eligibility: Financial creditor acting either by itself or jointly with other financial creditors.
Any other person notified by the Central Government acting on behalf of the financial creditor.

For financial creditors in a class under Section 21(6A)(a) or (b): application must be filed jointly by not less than 100 such creditors or not less than 10% of the total number of such creditors in the same class, whichever is less.

For financial creditors who are allottees under a real estate project: application must be filed jointly by not less than 100 such allottees or not less than 10% of the total number of such allottees under the same real estate project, whichever is less.
mandatory_prerequisites: Filing of application in prescribed form, manner, and accompanied by the prescribed fee.
Submission of record of default recorded with the information utility or other specified record/evidence of default.
Proposal of the name of an insolvency professional to act as interim resolution professional.
Any other information as specified by the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India.
statutory_bars: Adjudicating Authority is satisfied that default has not occurred.
Application filed under sub-section (2) is incomplete.
Disciplinary proceeding is pending against the proposed interim resolution professional.
Failure to meet mandatory class or real estate allottee quorum thresholds.
saving_exceptions: Adjudicating Authority must give notice to the applicant to rectify defects in the application within 7 days of receipt of notice prior to rejecting an incomplete application.
Record of default in respect of financial debt owed to a financial institution recorded with information utility is considered sufficient proof to ascertain existence of default.
Where statutory requirements under Section 7(5)(a) are complied with, no other ground shall be considered to reject the application.

section_title: Insolvency resolution by operational creditor
statutory_summary: Establishes the mandatory pre-initiation procedure for operational creditors, requiring the delivery of a demand notice or invoice to the corporate debtor upon default. Grants the corporate debtor 10 days to notify the creditor of a pre-existing dispute or provide proof of payment.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether a valid demand notice or invoice was delivered by the operational creditor, and whether the corporate debtor raised a valid pre-existing dispute or provided evidence of payment within the statutory 10-day period.

applicant_eligibility: An operational creditor upon the occurrence of a default.
mandatory_prerequisites: Delivery of a demand notice of unpaid operational debt or a copy of an invoice demanding payment of the amount involved in the default.
Notice must be delivered to the corporate debtor in the prescribed form and manner.
statutory_bars: Corporate debtor brings to notice the existence of a dispute or record of the pendency of a suit or arbitration proceedings filed before the receipt of the notice or invoice.
Corporate debtor proves payment of the unpaid operational debt by sending an attested copy of the record of electronic transfer.
Corporate debtor proves payment by sending an attested copy of a record that the operational creditor has encashed a cheque issued by the corporate debtor.

section_title: Application for initiation of corporate insolvency resolution process by operational creditor
statutory_summary: Permits an operational creditor to file an application to initiate CIRP against a corporate debtor after 10 days from serving a Section 8 demand notice, provided no payment or notice of dispute has been received.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the operational creditor delivered a valid Section 8 notice or invoice, whether the corporate debtor failed to pay or raise a pre-existing dispute, whether the application is complete, and whether any disciplinary proceeding is pending against the proposed IRP.

applicant_eligibility: Operational creditor who delivered a demand notice or invoice under Section 8(1) and did not receive payment or notice of dispute within 10 days.
mandatory_prerequisites: Copy of the invoice demanding payment or demand notice delivered to the corporate debtor.
Affidavit confirming no notice of dispute was given by the corporate debtor.
Copy of certificate from financial institutions maintaining accounts of the operational creditor confirming non-payment (if available).
Copy of record with information utility confirming non-payment (if available).
Any other proof or specified information confirming non-payment of unpaid operational debt.
statutory_bars: Application filed under sub-section (2) is incomplete.
Payment of the unpaid operational debt has been made by the corporate debtor.
Failure to deliver the invoice or demand notice for payment to the corporate debtor.
Notice of dispute received by the operational creditor or record of dispute exists in the information utility.
Disciplinary proceeding is pending against the proposed interim resolution professional.
saving_exceptions: Adjudicating Authority must give notice to the applicant to rectify defects in the application within seven days of receipt of notice prior to rejecting an incomplete application.

section_title: Initiation of corporate insolvency resolution process by corporate applicant
statutory_summary: Permits a corporate applicant of a corporate debtor that has committed a default to initiate the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) by filing an application along with financial documents and a special resolution of shareholders or a three-fourths partner resolution.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the corporate debtor has committed a default, whether the corporate applicant has provided the requisite corporate authorization (special resolution or 3/4th partner resolution) along with books of account, and whether the application is complete.

applicant_eligibility: Corporate applicant of a corporate debtor that has committed a default.
mandatory_prerequisites: Filing of application in prescribed form, manner, and accompanied with prescribed fee.
Information relating to books of account, specified documents, and other specified information.
Special resolution passed by shareholders of the corporate debtor or resolution passed by at least three-fourths of total partners of the corporate debtor approving the filing of the application.
statutory_bars: Application filed under sub-section (1) is incomplete.
Failure to obtain or furnish the requisite special resolution of shareholders or 3/4th partner resolution.
Corporate debtor or corporate applicant is disqualified under Section 11.
saving_exceptions: Adjudicating Authority must give notice to the applicant to rectify defects in the application within seven days from the date of receipt of notice prior to rejecting an incomplete application.

section_title: Persons not entitled to make application
statutory_summary: Lists statutory disqualifications that prohibit specific corporate debtors, financial creditors, operational creditors, or corporate applicants from initiating a Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP).
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the applicant or corporate debtor falls within any of the statutory bars listed under Section 11, such as being in ongoing insolvency proceedings, having completed CIRP or PPIRP within the preceding 12 months, having violated an approved resolution plan, or being subject to a liquidation order.

applicant_eligibility: Any entity or creditor seeking to initiate CIRP under Section 7, 9, or 10 must not be subject to the statutory disqualifications enumerated in Section 11.
mandatory_prerequisites: Verification that the applicant and corporate debtor are free from disqualifications specified under clauses (a) to (d).
statutory_bars: A corporate debtor currently undergoing CIRP or PPIRP.
A financial creditor or operational creditor of a corporate debtor currently undergoing PPIRP.
A corporate debtor that completed CIRP twelve months preceding the date of making the application.
A corporate debtor in respect of whom a resolution plan was approved under Chapter III-A twelve months preceding the date of making the application.
A corporate debtor or financial creditor who has violated any terms of an approved resolution plan twelve months before the date of making the application.
A corporate debtor in respect of whom a liquidation order has been made.
saving_exceptions: Under Explanation II, nothing in Section 11 prevents a corporate debtor referred to in clauses (a) to (d) from initiating CIRP against another corporate debtor.

section_title: Time-limit for completion of insolvency resolution process
statutory_summary: Establishes a mandatory 180-day time limit for completing the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP), permits a one-time extension of up to 90 days upon 66% CoC approval, and sets a mandatory outer limit of 330 days including legal proceedings.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the CIRP cannot be completed within 180 days due to the nature of the case, whether the extension application is backed by a 66% CoC vote, whether an extension has already been granted, and whether the process duration exceeds the mandatory outer limit of 330 days.

applicant_eligibility: Resolution professional instructed to seek an extension by a resolution passed at a meeting of the committee of creditors by a vote of sixty-six per cent of the voting shares.
mandatory_prerequisites: Approval of the committee of creditors by a vote of not less than sixty-six per cent of voting shares.
Filing of an application by the resolution professional to the Adjudicating Authority seeking extension beyond one hundred and eighty days.
statutory_bars: Extension of the CIRP period granted more than once under Section 12(3).
Exceeding the mandatory outer limit of three hundred and thirty days from the insolvency commencement date, including extensions and legal proceedings.
saving_exceptions: One-time extension of CIRP duration beyond 180 days by a further period not exceeding 90 days if the Adjudicating Authority is satisfied that the process cannot be completed within 180 days.
Pending CIRPs not completed within 330 days at the commencement of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Act, 2019 granted a 90-day completion window from such commencement date.

section_title: Withdrawal of application admitted under section 7, 9 or 10
statutory_summary: Permits the Adjudicating Authority to allow the withdrawal of an admitted CIRP application under Section 7, 9, or 10 upon an application by the resolution professional backed by ninety per cent voting share approval of the committee of creditors.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the resolution professional has obtained ninety per cent voting share approval from the committee of creditors for withdrawal, and whether the application is submitted after the constitution of the committee of creditors but before the issuance of the first invitation for resolution plans.

applicant_eligibility: Resolution professional submitting the application with the approval of ninety per cent voting share of the committee of creditors.
mandatory_prerequisites: Approval of ninety per cent voting share of the committee of creditors in such manner as specified.
Application for withdrawal made directly by the resolution professional to the Adjudicating Authority.
statutory_bars: Withdrawal sought before the constitution of the committee of creditors under sub-section (1) of section 21.
Withdrawal sought after the first invitation for submission of a resolution plan has been issued by the resolution professional.

section_title: Declaration of moratorium and public announcement
statutory_summary: Mandates that upon admitting a CIRP application under Section 7, 9, or 10, the Adjudicating Authority must issue an order declaring a moratorium, causing a public announcement calling for claims, and appointing an interim resolution professional.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether an application under Section 7, Section 9, or Section 10 has been formally admitted, triggering the mandatory statutory requirement to declare a moratorium, order a public announcement, and appoint an interim resolution professional.

applicant_eligibility: Adjudicating Authority acting consequential to the admission of an application under Section 7, Section 9, or Section 10.
mandatory_prerequisites: Formal admission of a CIRP application under Section 7, Section 9, or Section 10 by the Adjudicating Authority.
Issuance of an order declaring a moratorium pursuant to Section 14.
Issuance of an order appointing an interim resolution professional in the manner laid down in Section 16.
Public announcement of the initiation of CIRP and call for submission of claims under Section 15 to be made immediately after the appointment of the interim resolution professional.
statutory_bars: Non-admission or rejection of the underlying application under Section 7, Section 9, or Section 10.

section_title: Moratorium
statutory_summary: Declares a mandatory moratorium upon CIRP commencement, prohibiting legal suits, asset transfers, security enforcement, and property recovery against the corporate debtor, while protecting statutory grants and critical supplies subject to payment of current dues.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether a suit, legal proceeding, execution, asset transfer, or security enforcement is barred by the moratorium order, whether an exception applies (e.g., personal guarantor or notified transaction), or whether critical/essential supplies or statutory grants can be suspended due to non-payment of current dues during the moratorium.

applicant_eligibility: Corporate debtor protected automatically upon the admission of a CIRP application under Section 7, 9, or 10.
mandatory_prerequisites: Order of moratorium declared by the Adjudicating Authority on the insolvency commencement date.
Payment of current dues arising during the moratorium period for the continuation of essential/critical goods, services, or statutory licenses/permits.
statutory_bars: Institution of suits or continuation of pending suits or proceedings against the corporate debtor including execution of judgments, decrees, or orders.
Transferring, encumbering, alienating, or disposing of corporate debtor assets or legal/beneficial rights.
Any action to foreclose, recover, or enforce security interest created by the corporate debtor, including under the SARFAESI Act, 2002.
Recovery of property by an owner or lessor where such property is occupied by or in possession of the corporate debtor.
Action or proceeding by a surety against the corporate debtor pursuant to a contract of guarantee during moratorium.
saving_exceptions: Transactions, agreements, or arrangements notified by the Central Government in consultation with financial sector regulators.
Actions against a surety in a contract of guarantee to a corporate debtor.
Termination or suspension of critical/essential supplies or statutory grants/licenses if the corporate debtor defaults on current dues arising during the moratorium period.

section_title: Public announcement of corporate insolvency resolution process
statutory_summary: Mandates the publication and specifies the required contents of the public announcement of the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP), including details of the corporate debtor, claim submission deadline, IRP details, penalties for false claims, and CIRP closing date.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the public announcement was made in the specified manner and contains all mandatory statutory information, including corporate debtor details, claim deadlines, IRP particulars, and the CIRP completion date.

applicant_eligibility: Interim resolution professional appointed under Section 16 pursuant to an order of admission under Section 13.
mandatory_prerequisites: Inclusion of the name and address of the corporate debtor under CIRP.
Inclusion of the name of the authority with which the corporate debtor is incorporated or registered.
Inclusion of the last date for submission of claims as specified.
Inclusion of details of the interim resolution professional vested with management and responsible for receiving claims.
Inclusion of notice regarding penalties for false or misleading claims.
Inclusion of the CIRP closing date, set as the 180th day from the admission of the application under Section 7, 9, or 10.
Public announcement must be made in the manner specified by the Board.
statutory_bars: Omission of mandatory details required under sub-section (1) or non-compliance with the specified publication manner under sub-section (2).

section_title: Appointment and tenure of interim resolution professional
statutory_summary: Governs the appointment procedure, eligibility verification, reference mechanisms to the Board (IBBI), and tenure of the Interim Resolution Professional (IRP) upon CIRP commencement.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether any disciplinary proceeding is pending against the proposed interim resolution professional, or whether a reference to the Board is required for recommending an eligible insolvency professional.

applicant_eligibility: Adjudicating Authority appointing an Interim Resolution Professional on the insolvency commencement date.
mandatory_prerequisites: Appointment of the interim resolution professional on the insolvency commencement date.
For financial creditor applications under Section 7, appointment of the proposed RP if no disciplinary proceedings are pending against him.
For operational creditor applications under Section 9 with a proposed IRP, appointment of the proposed RP if no disciplinary proceedings are pending against him.
For operational creditor applications with no proposed IRP or corporate applicant applications under Section 10, mandatory reference by the Adjudicating Authority to the Board for recommendation.
Recommendation by the Board of an insolvency professional with no pending disciplinary proceedings within 10 days of receiving a reference.
statutory_bars: Pending disciplinary proceedings against the proposed insolvency professional.

section_title: Management of affairs of corporate debtor by interim resolution professional
statutory_summary: Vests the management of the corporate debtor in the interim resolution professional, suspends the powers of the board of directors or partners, mandates corporate personnel and financial institutions to follow IRP instructions, and grants the IRP access to records and authority over legal compliances.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the management of the corporate debtor stands vested in the IRP, whether powers of the board or partners are suspended, and whether officers, managers, or financial institutions are failing to comply with IRP instructions or provide access to records.

applicant_eligibility: Interim resolution professional appointed under Section 16 upon admission of CIRP.
mandatory_prerequisites: Vesting of the management of affairs of the corporate debtor in the interim resolution professional from the date of appointment.
Suspension of powers of the board of directors or partners of the corporate debtor.
Reporting of officers and managers to the interim resolution professional with full access to documents and records.
Mandatory compliance by financial institutions maintaining corporate debtor accounts with IRP instructions.
statutory_bars: Exercise of corporate or managerial powers by the suspended board of directors or partners after IRP appointment.
Refusal or delay by officers, managers, statutory auditors, or financial institutions to extend cooperation or provide access to records and bank accounts.

section_title: Duties of interim resolution professional
statutory_summary: Outlines the mandatory duties of the Interim Resolution Professional (IRP), including asset and operational data collection, receiving, collating, and verifying creditor claims, constituting the Committee of Creditors, managing operations, and taking custody of assets owned by the corporate debtor.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the interim resolution professional has fulfilled statutory duties—including claim collation/verification, Committee of Creditors constitution, and taking control over corporate debtor assets—without impermissibly taking custody of third-party or subsidiary assets.

applicant_eligibility: Interim resolution professional appointed under Section 16 upon admission of CIRP.
mandatory_prerequisites: Collection of asset, financial, and operational information for the previous two years.
Receiving, collating, verifying, and determining the value of creditor claims pursuant to public announcement under Sections 13 and 15.
Constitution of the Committee of Creditors.
Taking custody and control of tangible, intangible, foreign, and security assets over which the corporate debtor has ownership rights.
statutory_bars: Taking control or custody of assets owned by a third party held under trust or contractual arrangement (including bailment).
Taking control or custody of assets belonging to any Indian or foreign subsidiary of the corporate debtor.
Taking control or custody of assets notified by the Central Government in consultation with a financial sector regulator.

section_title: Persons to extend cooperation to interim resolution professional
statutory_summary: Mandates that current or former personnel, promoters, management associates, or contractual service providers of the corporate debtor extend all assistance and cooperation to the IRP or RP, and empowers the Adjudicating Authority to issue compliance orders upon an application detailing non-cooperation.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the person from whom assistance or cooperation is sought falls under the statutory scope of Section 19(1) and whether that person has failed or refused to cooperate with the interim resolution professional or resolution professional.

applicant_eligibility: Interim resolution professional or resolution professional appointed under Chapter II.
mandatory_prerequisites: Target person is or has been personnel, promoter, associated with management, or engaged in a contract for service with the corporate debtor.
Failure or refusal by such person to assist or cooperate with the IRP or RP in managing affairs or performing statutory duties.
Filing of an application by the IRP or RP to the Adjudicating Authority for necessary directions under Section 19(2).
statutory_bars: Respondent is not a person covered under Section 19(1) or otherwise required to assist or cooperate with the IRP or RP.

section_title: Management of operations of corporate debtor as going concern
statutory_summary: Mandates the interim resolution professional to make every endeavour to protect and preserve the value of the property of the corporate debtor and manage its operations as a going concern, providing explicit statutory authorities regarding professional appointments, contract modifications, raising interim finance, and issuing personnel instructions.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the interim resolution professional acted within statutory authority to preserve property value and maintain the corporate debtor as a going concern, and whether required creditor consent was obtained when creating security interests over encumbered assets to raise interim finance.

applicant_eligibility: Interim resolution professional appointed under Section 16 upon the commencement of CIRP.
mandatory_prerequisites: Duty to protect and preserve the value of the property of the corporate debtor.
Duty to manage the operations of the corporate debtor as a going concern.

Obtaining prior consent of creditors whose debt is secured over encumbered property before creating a security interest over such property to raise interim finance, unless the value of the property is at least twice the debt amount.
statutory_bars: Creating a security interest over encumbered property for interim finance without prior consent of secured creditors when the value of the property is less than twice the debt amount.
saving_exceptions: Prior consent of the secured creditor is not required for creating a security interest over encumbered property if the value of such property is not less than the amount equivalent to twice the amount of the debt.

section_title: Committee of creditors
statutory_summary: Mandates the constitution of the Committee of Creditors (CoC) comprising all non-related party financial creditors, specifies voting share determination, establishes mechanisms for class representation by authorised representatives, sets the default decision threshold at 51% voting share, and extends CoC supervision to the liquidation process.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the CoC has been properly constituted with eligible financial creditors, whether related party financial creditors have been excluded (or validly saved under the debt-to-equity conversion proviso), whether authorised representatives were properly appointed for class creditors, and whether decisions meet the statutory voting threshold.

applicant_eligibility: All financial creditors of the corporate debtor to whom financial debt is owed.
Regulated financial creditors who are related parties solely due to pre-ICD debt-to-equity conversions or substitutions.
Authorised representatives appointed to represent classes of financial creditors, security holders, deposit holders, or minor/incapacitated creditors.
mandatory_prerequisites: Collation of all claims received and determination of financial position by the interim resolution professional prior to constituting the CoC.

Filing of an application by the IRP to the Adjudicating Authority for the appointment of an Authorised Representative where financial debt is owed to a class of creditors exceeding the specified number.
Determination of voting share based on the proportion of financial debt owed to each financial creditor relative to total financial debt owed to eligible CoC members.
Mandatory minimum threshold of 51% voting share for standard CoC decisions, unless a higher threshold is specified by another provision of the Code.
RP must furnish financial information requested by the CoC within seven days of requisition.
statutory_bars: Financial creditors or their authorised representatives who are related parties of the corporate debtor are barred from representation, participation, or voting in CoC meetings.
Financial creditors holding operational debt assigned/transferred from operational creditors are treated as operational creditors for that debt and excluded from financial creditor voting share.
saving_exceptions: The related party bar does not apply to a financial creditor regulated by a financial sector regulator if it became a related party solely on account of conversion or substitution of debt into equity shares or convertible instruments prior to the insolvency commencement date.
Where a corporate debtor has no financial creditors, the CoC shall be constituted comprising specified persons (such as operational creditors or workmen) to exercise specified functions.

section_title: Appointment of resolution professional
statutory_summary: Mandates holding the first CoC meeting within seven days of constitution to decide, by a minimum 66% voting share of financial creditors, whether to retain the IRP as Resolution Professional or replace them, subject to written consent and Board confirmation.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the Committee of Creditors approved the continuation or replacement of the interim resolution professional by at least 66% voting share, submitted the written consent in the specified form, and obtained Board confirmation for any proposed replacement.

applicant_eligibility: Committee of Creditors voting in its first meeting by a majority of not less than sixty-six per cent of the voting share of financial creditors.
mandatory_prerequisites: Holding the first meeting of the committee of creditors within seven days of its constitution.
Resolution passed by a majority of not less than sixty-six per cent of the voting share of financial creditors.
Submission of written consent from the continuing or proposed resolution professional in the specified form.
Communication of decision to continue the IRP as RP to the IRP, the corporate debtor, and the Board.
Filing an application before the Adjudicating Authority with written consent if replacing the IRP, followed by forwarding the proposed RP's name to the Board for confirmation.
statutory_bars: Failure to obtain the mandatory sixty-six per cent voting share of financial creditors.
Absence of written consent in the specified form from the proposed or continuing resolution professional.
saving_exceptions: Where the Board does not confirm the proposed RP within ten days of receipt, the Adjudicating Authority shall order the IRP to continue functioning as RP until confirmation is granted.

section_title: Resolution professional to conduct corporate insolvency resolution process
statutory_summary: Mandates the resolution professional to conduct the entire CIRP and manage the operations of the corporate debtor during and beyond the CIRP period until an order approving the resolution plan or appointing a liquidator is passed.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the resolution professional is properly conducting the CIRP and managing corporate debtor operations, whether management authority extends pending final orders under Section 31 or Section 34, and whether a replaced IRP has handed over all records.

applicant_eligibility: Resolution professional appointed under Section 22 or Section 27 during the corporate insolvency resolution process.
mandatory_prerequisites: Conduct the entire corporate insolvency resolution process and manage the operations of the corporate debtor during the CIRP period.
Exercise powers and perform duties vested or conferred on the interim resolution professional under Chapter II.

Mandatory handover by the interim resolution professional of all information, documents, and records pertaining to the corporate debtor upon appointment of the resolution professional under Section 22(4).

Continued management of operations of the corporate debtor after the expiry of the CIRP period until an order approving the resolution plan under Section 31(1) or appointing a liquidator under Section 34 is passed.
statutory_bars: Interim resolution professional failing or refusing to provide information, documents, and records in possession and knowledge to the newly appointed resolution professional.
saving_exceptions: Resolution professional continues to manage operations after expiry of the CIRP period until the Adjudicating Authority passes an order approving a resolution plan under Section 31(1) or appointing a liquidator under Section 34.

section_title: Meeting of committee of creditors
statutory_summary: Regulates the convening, notice requirements, participation rights, representation, voting share determination, and conduct of Committee of Creditors (CoC) meetings managed by the resolution professional.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether meetings of the Committee of Creditors were properly convened and conducted by the resolution professional, whether mandatory notices were served on all required participants (including eligible operational creditors and suspended directors/partners), and whether voting rights were accurately assigned and exercised.

applicant_eligibility: Resolution professional responsible for conducting all CoC meetings.
Members of the Committee of Creditors, including authorised representatives.
Members of the suspended Board of Directors or partners of the corporate debtor.
Operational creditors or their representative if aggregate operational dues are not less than ten per cent of total debt.
mandatory_prerequisites: All meetings of the committee of creditors must be conducted by the resolution professional.

Notice of each CoC meeting must be given to CoC members (including authorised representatives), suspended directors/partners, and operational creditors holding at least ten per cent of aggregate debt.
Resolution professional must determine and assign voting share to each financial creditor in the specified manner.
Voting must be conducted strictly in accordance with assigned voting shares.
statutory_bars: Directors, partners, and the representative of operational creditors are strictly barred from voting in CoC meetings.
A creditor cannot appoint the current resolution professional as their individual representative IP.
saving_exceptions: Absence of any director, partner, or representative of operational creditors does not invalidate the proceedings of a CoC meeting.

section_title: Duties of resolution professional
statutory_summary: Outlines the fundamental duties and explicit statutory powers of the Resolution Professional (RP) to preserve and protect corporate debtor assets, maintain business operations, prepare information memorandums, invite and present resolution plans, and file applications for avoidance transactions or fraudulent/wrongful trading.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the resolution professional has fulfilled statutory obligations—including taking custody of assets, maintaining updated claim lists, issuing invitations for resolution plans based on CoC-approved criteria, and applying to the Adjudicating Authority for avoidance transactions or fraudulent/wrongful trading.

applicant_eligibility: Resolution professional appointed under Section 22 or Section 27 to conduct the corporate insolvency resolution process.
mandatory_prerequisites: Duty to preserve and protect all assets and continued business operations of the corporate debtor.
Taking immediate custody and control of all assets and business records of the corporate debtor.
Representing the corporate debtor in legal, quasi-judicial, or arbitration proceedings.
Maintaining an updated list of claims.
Convening and attending all meetings of the committee of creditors.
Preparing the information memorandum in accordance with Section 29.
Inviting prospective resolution applicants based on criteria laid down with the prior approval of the committee of creditors.
Presenting all compliant resolution plans at meetings of the committee of creditors.
Filing applications to the Adjudicating Authority in respect of avoidance transactions or fraudulent/wrongful trading.
statutory_bars: Raising interim finance without the prior approval of the committee of creditors under Section 28.
Inviting prospective resolution applicants without obtaining prior approval of the eligibility criteria from the committee of creditors.

section_title: Rights and duties of authorised representative of financial creditors
statutory_summary: Defines the rights and duties of an authorised representative (AR) of financial creditors, including participation and voting in CoC meetings, circulating agenda/minutes, filing voting instructions, and applying the class majority rule (>50% of cast votes) for Section 21(6A) creditors except on Section 12A withdrawal applications.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the authorised representative acted in accordance with statutory voting mandates—applying the >50% class majority rule for Section 21(6A) creditors or individual split voting for Section 12A applications—and fulfilled procedural duties to circulate agenda/minutes and record voting instructions with the CoC.

applicant_eligibility: Authorised representative appointed under sub-section (6) or sub-section (6A) of section 21 or sub-section (5) of section 24.
mandatory_prerequisites: Duty to circulate the agenda and minutes of CoC meetings to represented financial creditors.
Obtaining prior voting instructions from financial creditors through physical or electronic means.
For Section 21(6A) ARs, casting vote on behalf of all represented financial creditors in accordance with the decision of more than fifty per cent of the voting share of creditors who cast their vote.
Duty to file physical or electronic voting instructions received from financial creditors with the committee of creditors.
statutory_bars: Authorised representative acting against the interest of the financial creditors represented.
Failing to abstain from voting on behalf of an individual financial creditor who has not provided prior voting instructions under the Section 25A(3) voting mechanism.
saving_exceptions: For Section 21(6A) authorised representatives, the vote of all represented creditors is cast as a single block based on the decision of >50% of voting share of creditors who cast their vote.
For voting on Section 12A withdrawal applications, Section 21(6A) ARs are carved out from the block voting rule and must cast votes individually per creditor instruction under Section 25A(3).

section_title: Replacement of resolution professional by committee of creditors
statutory_summary: Empowers the committee of creditors to replace an existing resolution professional at any time during CIRP by a vote of sixty-six per cent of voting shares, subject to written consent from the proposed RP and confirmation by the Board.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the resolution to replace the resolution professional was passed by at least sixty-six per cent of voting shares of the committee of creditors, accompanied by written consent in the specified form, and whether any disciplinary proceedings are pending against the proposed resolution professional.

applicant_eligibility: Committee of creditors acting by a vote of sixty-six per cent of voting shares.
mandatory_prerequisites: Resolution passed at a meeting of the committee of creditors by a vote of sixty-six per cent of voting shares.
Written consent from the proposed resolution professional in the specified form.
Forwarding of the proposed resolution professional's name by the committee of creditors to the Adjudicating Authority.
Forwarding of the proposed name by the Adjudicating Authority to the Board for confirmation.
statutory_bars: Failure to obtain the required sixty-six per cent voting share of the committee of creditors.
Pending disciplinary proceedings against the proposed resolution professional.
Absence of written consent in the specified form from the proposed resolution professional.
saving_exceptions: Where disciplinary proceedings are pending against the proposed resolution professional, the resolution professional appointed under section 22 shall continue until another resolution professional is appointed under this section.

section_title: Approval of committee of creditors for certain actions
statutory_summary: Restricts the resolution professional from taking specific critical management, financial, structural, or legal actions during CIRP without prior approval of the committee of creditors by a vote of sixty-six per cent of voting shares, declaring any unapproved action void.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the resolution professional took any enumerated action under Section 28(1) without convening a meeting and obtaining prior approval from the committee of creditors by a sixty-six per cent voting share.

applicant_eligibility: Resolution professional seeking prior approval for actions enumerated under sub-section (1).
Committee of creditors reporting unapproved actions of the resolution professional to the Board.
mandatory_prerequisites: Resolution professional must convene a meeting of the committee of creditors prior to taking any action listed under sub-section (1).
Obtaining prior approval passed by a vote of not less than sixty-six per cent of voting shares of the financial creditors.

Seeking prior approval for actions including raising excess interim finance, creating security interests, changing capital structure, modifying ownership/management, entering related party transactions, delegating authority, or altering auditor/personnel contracts.
statutory_bars: Taking any action enumerated under Section 28(1) without seeking and obtaining prior approval of the committee of creditors.
Action supported by less than sixty-six per cent of the voting shares of the committee of creditors.

section_title: Person not eligible to be resolution applicant
statutory_summary: Prescribes comprehensive negative eligibility criteria that render a person, persons acting jointly or in concert, or connected persons ineligible to submit a resolution plan during corporate insolvency resolution process.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether a resolution applicant, any person acting jointly or in concert with them, or any connected person falls under any statutory disqualifications specified under clauses (a) to (j) of Section 29A.

applicant_eligibility: Resolution applicant submitting a plan individually or jointly pursuant to invitation under Section 25(2)(h) or Section 54K.
Must not suffer from any personal disqualification under clauses (a) to (i) or have any connected person suffering from such disqualification under clause (j).
mandatory_prerequisites: Filing of an affidavit along with the resolution plan declaring eligibility under Section 29A.
Mandatory verification of eligibility of the resolution applicant and all connected persons by the resolution professional and committee of creditors.
statutory_bars: Is an undischarged insolvent.
Is a wilful defaulter under RBI guidelines.
Has an account classified as a non-performing asset (NPA) for at least one year prior to CIRP commencement date.
Has been convicted of an offence punishable with imprisonment for two years or more under the Twelfth Schedule, or seven years or more under any other law.
Is disqualified to act as a director under the Companies Act, 2013.
Is prohibited by SEBI from trading in securities or accessing securities markets.

Was a promoter or in management/control of a corporate debtor where avoidance orders for preferential, undervalued, extortionate credit, or fraudulent transactions were made by the Adjudicating Authority.
Has executed an invoked and unpaid guarantee in favour of a creditor in respect of a corporate debtor under CIRP.
Is subject to any disability corresponding to clauses (a) to (h) under foreign jurisdiction law.
Has a connected person (promoter, management/control, holding/subsidiary/associate company, or related party) ineligible under clauses (a) to (i).
saving_exceptions: NPA disqualification under clause (c) is cured if the applicant pays all overdue amounts with interest and charges prior to submitting the resolution plan.
NPA disqualification does not apply to a financial entity resolution applicant that is not a related party to the corporate debtor.
NPA disqualification does not apply for three years if the NPA account was acquired pursuant to a prior approved resolution plan under the Code.
Criminal conviction bar under clause (d) lapses after two years from release from imprisonment.

Avoidance transaction bar under clause (g) does not apply if transactions occurred prior to acquisition of the corporate debtor under a prior approved resolution plan/scheme without contribution by the applicant.
Disqualification exceptions for connected persons apply to non-related party financial entities.

section_title: Submission of resolution plan
statutory_summary: Regulates the submission of resolution plans, mandatory compliance checks by the resolution professional, mandatory payout protections for operational and dissenting financial creditors, and the 66% voting threshold for Committee of Creditors approval.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the resolution plan satisfies all statutory conditions under Section 30(2)—including Section 29A eligibility, priority payment of CIRP costs, operational and dissenting financial creditor statutory minimums, feasibility and viability, and non-contravention of law—and has been approved by at least 66% voting share of the Committee of Creditors.

applicant_eligibility: Resolution applicant submitting a resolution plan individually or jointly pursuant to the information memorandum.
Must submit an affidavit confirming eligibility under Section 29A along with the resolution plan.
mandatory_prerequisites: Affidavit affirming Section 29A eligibility accompanying the resolution plan.
Priority payment of insolvency resolution process costs.
Payment of debts to operational creditors that is not less than the higher of liquidation value under Section 53 or plan distribution value under Section 53 priority.
Payment of debts to dissenting financial creditors that is not less than the lower of liquidation value under Section 53 or plan distribution value under Section 53 priority.
Provisions for post-approval management of the corporate debtor.
Provisions for implementation and supervision of the resolution plan, including monitoring committee constitution.
Plan does not contravene any provision of law for the time being in force.
Approval by the Committee of Creditors by a vote of not less than sixty-six per cent of voting share of financial creditors.
Committee of Creditors recording reasons for approval after evaluating feasibility, viability, manner of distribution, and security interest value.
Submission of the approved resolution plan by the resolution professional to the Adjudicating Authority.
statutory_bars: Ineligibility of the resolution applicant under Section 29A.
Failure to provide priority payment for CIRP costs.
Operational creditor payout below statutory minimum threshold.
Dissenting financial creditor payout below statutory minimum threshold.
Resolution plan contravenes any law in force.
Approval by Committee of Creditors with less than sixty-six per cent voting share.
saving_exceptions: Deemed shareholder approval under the Companies Act, 2013 or other laws for actions required under the resolution plan.
A period not exceeding thirty days allowed to resolution applicants ineligible under Section 29A(c) to pay overdue amounts with interest to cure ineligibility.
Section 30(2)(ba) protections under Amendment Act 2026 do not apply to CIRP proceedings where CoC approval or liquidation orders occurred prior to the commencement of the 2026 Act.

section_title: Approval of resolution plan
statutory_summary: Governs the judicial approval or rejection of a CoC-approved resolution plan by the Adjudicating Authority, making it binding on all stakeholders (including government authorities), extinguishing past unprovided claims, terminating moratorium, and protecting statutory grants and licenses during subsistence.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the CoC-approved resolution plan satisfies Section 30(2) requirements and contains provisions for effective implementation, whether required Competition Commission of India (CCI) approvals were obtained prior to submission under Section 30(6), and whether prior claims against the corporate debtor stand extinguished upon approval.

applicant_eligibility: Resolution professional submitting the CoC-approved resolution plan under Section 30(6).
mandatory_prerequisites: Satisfaction of the Adjudicating Authority that the resolution plan meets Section 30(2) requirements and has provisions for effective implementation.
Prior approval of the Competition Commission of India under the Competition Act, 2002 if the plan involves a combination, obtained before submission to the Adjudicating Authority.
Statutory approval of plan implementation by Adjudicating Authority within 30 days of receipt.
Obtaining other statutory/regulatory approvals required under any law within one year from plan approval date or as provided by such law.
Forwarding of all CIRP records and resolution plan to the Board database by the resolution professional.
statutory_bars: Failure of the resolution plan to conform to requirements referred to in Section 30(2).
Failure to obtain Competition Commission of India approval before submitting the plan to the Adjudicating Authority.
Institution or continuation of proceedings against the corporate debtor or its assets on the basis of prior extinguished claims.
Suspension or termination of statutory licenses, permits, or grants by government authorities during the remaining subsistence period, provided current obligations are met.
saving_exceptions: Adjudicating Authority may give notice to the CoC to rectify defects in the resolution plan before rejecting it.
Adjudicating Authority may, on RP application backed by 66% CoC vote, first approve plan implementation and subsequently approve the distribution manner within 30 days.
Extinction of claims under Section 31(6) does not affect claims or proceedings against promoters, former management, guarantors, or co-debtors jointly/severally liable.

section_title: Liability for prior offences, etc.
statutory_summary: Grants statutory immunity to the corporate debtor and its assets from prosecution, attachment, seizure, or confiscation for offences committed prior to CIRP commencement, provided there is a complete change in management/control to an independent third party pursuant to an approved resolution plan or liquidation sale, while maintaining personal liability for defaulting officers and promoters.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the approval of a resolution plan under Section 31 or sale of liquidation assets under Chapter III results in a bona fide change of management or control to a person who is not a promoter, related party, or conspirator/abettor in the pre-CIRP offence, thereby entitling the corporate debtor and its property to statutory immunity from criminal prosecution and asset attachment.

applicant_eligibility: Corporate debtor or successful resolution applicant/acquirer taking over control of the corporate debtor or its assets pursuant to an approved resolution plan under Section 31 or liquidation sale under Chapter III.
mandatory_prerequisites: Approval of a resolution plan by the Adjudicating Authority under Section 31 or sale of liquidation assets under Chapter III.
Transfer of management or control of the corporate debtor/property to a person who was not a promoter, in management/control, or a related party of the corporate debtor prior to CIRP commencement.
Acquirer or new management must not be a person regarding whom investigating authorities have filed a report or complaint alleging abetment or conspiracy for the pre-CIRP offence.
Corporate debtor and associated persons must extend full assistance and co-operation to any authority investigating a pre-CIRP offence.
statutory_bars: New acquirer or management is a promoter, in management/control, or a related party of the pre-CIRP corporate debtor.
New acquirer or management is named in a report or complaint submitted to a court/authority as an abettor or conspirator in the offence.
Prohibition against statutory authorities taking action against corporate debtor property (attachment, seizure, retention, or confiscation) covered by an approved resolution plan or liquidation sale.
saving_exceptions: Designated partners, officers in default, promoters, or persons directly or indirectly involved in the pre-CIRP offence remain personally liable to be prosecuted and punished despite corporate debtor immunity.
Immunity does not bar actions against property owned by third parties or persons other than the qualifying acquirer/corporate debtor under applicable laws.

section_title: Initiation of liquidation
statutory_summary: Mandates the initiation of the liquidation process or dissolution of the corporate debtor upon CIRP expiry without an approved plan, plan rejection, 66% CoC decision, or plan contravention, while permitting a one-time restoration of CIRP for up to 120 days upon CoC application.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether statutory grounds for liquidation exist (non-receipt/rejection of resolution plan, 66% CoC vote, or plan contravention), whether the CoC has validly applied for a one-time CIRP restoration for up to 120 days under Section 33(1A), or whether CIRP should be reinstated following a plan contravention.

applicant_eligibility: Adjudicating Authority acting suo motu upon non-receipt of a plan under Section 30(6) or rejection under Section 31.
Resolution Professional intimating decision of the Committee of Creditors (passed by at least 66% voting share) to liquidate or dissolve the corporate debtor.
Committee of Creditors (by at least 66% voting share) applying for a one-time restoration of CIRP prior to issuance of a liquidation order.
Any person whose interests are prejudicially affected by a contravention of an approved resolution plan under Section 31 or Section 54L.
mandatory_prerequisites: Non-receipt of resolution plan prior to CIRP expiry or rejection of resolution plan under Section 31.
Or, intimation of CoC resolution passed by not less than sixty-six per cent of voting share to liquidate or dissolve the corporate debtor.
Or, application by an affected person establishing that the corporate debtor has contravened an approved resolution plan.
Passing of liquidation order requiring public announcement, notice to corporate registry, declaration of moratorium under Section 14(1)(a) & (c), and appointment of a liquidator under Section 34.
Adjudicating Authority must pass liquidation order within 30 days from receipt of intimation or application, recording reasons in writing if delayed.
statutory_bars: Bar on commencing or proceeding with any suit or legal proceeding by or against the corporate debtor post-liquidation order without leave of the Adjudicating Authority.
Restoration of CIRP under Section 33(1A) cannot be granted more than once.
saving_exceptions: CoC may, by a vote of at least sixty-six per cent of voting share, apply to restore CIRP for a duration not exceeding 120 days before a liquidation order is passed.
In case of plan contravention under Section 33(3), the Adjudicating Authority may reinstate CIRP instead of ordering liquidation.
Liquidation moratorium does not apply to transactions notified by the Central Government in consultation with financial sector regulators.
Liquidation order does not operate as a notice of discharge if the corporate debtor's business is continued during liquidation by the liquidator.

section_title: Appointment of liquidator and fee to be paid
statutory_summary: Governs the reference to the Board for recommending an insolvency professional as liquidator (strictly excluding the CIRP Resolution Professional), vesting of management powers in the liquidator, mandatory cooperation under Section 19 principles, record handover by the former RP, and determination/payment of liquidator fees under Section 53.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the insolvency professional proposed as liquidator was recommended by the Board (excluding the CIRP Resolution Professional) with written consent, whether powers of the board of directors/KMPs stand vested in the liquidator, and whether former CIRP RPs or corporate personnel fulfilled record transfer and cooperation obligations.

applicant_eligibility: Adjudicating Authority initiating liquidator appointment upon passing a liquidation order under Section 33.
Insolvency professional (other than the CIRP Resolution Professional) recommended by the Board with written consent.
mandatory_prerequisites: Reference by the Adjudicating Authority to the Board for recommending an insolvency professional upon passing a Section 33 liquidation order.
Proposal by the Board of an insolvency professional (other than the CIRP RP) along with written consent within ten days of reference.
Cessation of powers of the board of directors, key managerial personnel, and partners, with full vesting of powers in the liquidator upon appointment.
Mandatory forwarding of all CIRP records by the former resolution professional to the appointed liquidator.
Mandatory assistance and cooperation by personnel, promoters, management associates, and service providers under Section 19 mutatis mutandis.
Payment of liquidator fees from the proceeds of the liquidation estate in priority under Section 53.
statutory_bars: Strict statutory prohibition against appointing or replacing the CIRP Resolution Professional as the liquidator for the liquidation process of the corporate debtor.
Failure or refusal by corporate personnel or former management to extend assistance and cooperation to the liquidator.
Failure of former resolution professional to hand over all CIRP records to the liquidator.

section_title: Powers and duties of liquidator
statutory_summary: Enumerates the comprehensive statutory powers and duties of the liquidator to manage the liquidation estate, evaluate and sell assets, settle claims, continue or institute legal/avoidance proceedings, and distribute proceeds under the supervision of the committee of creditors.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the liquidator exercised statutory powers and performed duties within the framework of the Code—including asset custody, sale restrictions under Section 29A, avoidance transaction filings, claim settlement, and CoC supervision—subject to directions of the Adjudicating Authority.

applicant_eligibility: Liquidator appointed under Section 34 exercising statutory powers and performing duties during the liquidation process.
Committee of creditors supervising the conduct of the liquidation process under Section 35(2).
mandatory_prerequisites: Taking immediate custody and control of all assets, properties, effects, and actionable claims of the corporate debtor.
Evaluation of assets and preparation of valuation report in the manner specified by the Board.
Maintaining an updated list of claims of creditors in such manner as may be specified.
Selling property of the corporate debtor by public auction or private contract in accordance with specified regulations.
Supervision of the liquidation process by the committee of creditors in the specified manner.
Settling claims of creditors and distributing proceeds in accordance with the provisions of the Code (Section 53 priorities).
statutory_bars: Strict prohibition against selling immovable/movable property or actionable claims of the corporate debtor in liquidation to any person who is ineligible to be a resolution applicant under Section 29A.
saving_exceptions: Liquidator may carry on the business of the corporate debtor so far as may be necessary for its beneficial liquidation.
Amendments to clauses (a) and (j) of sub-section (1) made by the 2026 Amendment Act do not apply to liquidation and voluntary liquidation processes initiated on or before May 26, 2026.

section_title: Preferential transactions and relevant time
statutory_summary: Empowers the resolution professional or liquidator to apply to the Adjudicating Authority for avoidance of preferential transactions made for antecedent debts that place a creditor, surety, or guarantor in a better position than under Section 53 distribution within statutory look-back periods.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether a transfer of corporate debtor property/interest was made for an antecedent liability, resulted in a preferential position under Section 53, occurred within the relevant look-back period (1 year for non-related parties, 2 years for related parties), and whether it falls outside the ordinary course of business or new value exceptions.

applicant_eligibility: Resolution professional during corporate insolvency resolution process.
Liquidator during liquidation process.
mandatory_prerequisites: Transfer of property or an interest thereof of the corporate debtor for the benefit of a creditor, surety, or guarantor on account of an antecedent financial/operational debt or liability.
Transfer puts the transferee in a more beneficial position than they would have received under Section 53 distribution.

Transaction occurred within the relevant time: 2 years starting from preceding the initiation date to the insolvency commencement date for related parties (excluding employees), or 1 year for non-related parties.
statutory_bars: Transfer made in the ordinary course of business or financial affairs of the corporate debtor or the transferee.
Transfer creating a purchase-money security interest securing new value registered with an information utility within thirty days of the corporate debtor receiving possession.
saving_exceptions: Transfers made in pursuance of a court order are explicitly not protected and can still be declared as preferential transactions.

section_title: Avoidance of undervalued transactions
statutory_summary: Empowers the resolution professional or liquidator to apply to the Adjudicating Authority to declare transactions as void and reverse their effect if the corporate debtor gifted assets or transferred them for significantly undervalue outside the ordinary course of business during the relevant look-back period under Section 46.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the corporate debtor gifted assets or transferred them for consideration significantly less than the value of consideration provided by the corporate debtor, outside the ordinary course of business, during the relevant look-back period specified under Section 46.

applicant_eligibility: Resolution professional during corporate insolvency resolution process.
Liquidator during liquidation process.
mandatory_prerequisites: Transfer of one or more assets by the corporate debtor by way of gift or for consideration significantly less than the value of consideration provided by the corporate debtor.
Determination by the RP or liquidator that the transaction occurred within the relevant look-back period under Section 46.
Filing of an application before the Adjudicating Authority to declare such transaction void and reverse its effect.
statutory_bars: Transaction took place in the ordinary course of business of the corporate debtor.

section_title: Extortionate credit transactions
statutory_summary: Empowers the resolution professional or liquidator to apply to the Adjudicating Authority for avoidance of credit transactions involving financial or operational debt entered into within two years prior to the initiation date that required exorbitant payments by the corporate debtor.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the credit transaction required exorbitant payments by the corporate debtor during the two-year look-back period preceding the initiation date, and whether the provider is exempt as a law-compliant financial service provider.

applicant_eligibility: Resolution professional during corporate insolvency resolution process.
Liquidator during liquidation process.
mandatory_prerequisites: Corporate debtor was party to a credit transaction involving the receipt of financial or operational debt.
Terms of the transaction required exorbitant payments to be made by the corporate debtor.
Transaction took place during the period starting two years preceding the initiation date and ending on the insolvency commencement date.
Application made by the RP or liquidator to the Adjudicating Authority for avoidance under Section 50.
statutory_bars: Debt extended by any person providing financial services in compliance with any law for the time being in force shall in no event be considered an extortionate credit transaction.

section_title: Secured creditor in liquidation proceedings
statutory_summary: Provides secured creditors in liquidation the choice to either relinquish their security interest to the liquidation estate or realise it independently, subject to a 14-day notice window, 66% consent requirement among joint secured creditors, liquidator verification, mandatory deduction of process/workmen costs, and return of excess proceeds.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the secured creditor validly exercised its option to realise its security interest within the 14-day statutory period, obtained the requisite 66% consent from co-secured creditors where applicable, verified its security interest with the liquidator, and deducted/remitted mandatory CIRP, liquidation, and workmen costs to the liquidator.

applicant_eligibility: Secured creditor of the corporate debtor in liquidation proceedings.
mandatory_prerequisites: Secured creditor seeking to realise security interest must inform the liquidator and identify the specific asset within 14 days from the liquidation commencement date.

Agreement of secured creditors representing not less than sixty-six per cent of the value of all claims secured by the asset where multiple secured creditors hold security interest over the same asset.
Verification of security interest by the liquidator through Information Utility records or specified means before permitting realization.
Mandatory deduction of CIRP costs, liquidation costs, and workmen's dues under Section 53(1)(a) and 53(1)(b)(i) from realization proceeds and remittance of such amounts to the liquidator.
Accounting for and tendering any surplus realization proceeds beyond the debt due to the liquidator.
statutory_bars: Failure to inform liquidator and identify asset within 14 days results in deemed relinquishment of the security interest to the liquidation estate.
Prohibition on realization where multiple secured creditors exist unless approved by secured creditors representing at least sixty-six per cent of secured claim value.
saving_exceptions: Secured creditor facing resistance in taking possession or selling the asset may apply to the Adjudicating Authority for facilitating realisation.
Unpaid debt balance following realization is paid by the liquidator under the priority specified in Section 53(1)(e).
Sub-section (2) as amended by the Amendment Act, 2026 does not apply to liquidation processes initiated on or before May 26, 2026.

section_title: Distribution of assets
statutory_summary: Establishes a mandatory waterfall hierarchy for distributing liquidation asset proceeds overriding all other laws, prioritizing CIRP/liquidation costs, workmen dues and relinquished secured debts, employee wages, unsecured financial debts, statutory government dues/unpaid secured balances, remaining debts, and equity/preference shareholders.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the liquidator distributed liquidation proceeds in strict compliance with the statutory waterfall hierarchy under Section 53(1), correctly categorized claims and security values, proportionately deducted fees, and disregarded contractual arrangements that attempt to alter inter-class statutory priority.

applicant_eligibility: Liquidator distributing proceeds of the liquidation estate under Chapter III.
Creditors, workmen, employees, government authorities, and shareholders entitled to distribution under the statutory waterfall.
mandatory_prerequisites: Full payment of CIRP costs and liquidation costs under clause (a) in priority to all other claims.
Equal ranking and pari passu distribution among claims within the same sub-clause (e.g., workmen dues for 24 months and relinquished secured debt under clause (b)).
Limiting secured creditor priority under clause (b)(ii) to the determined value of the relinquished security interest, with any remaining balance treated as unsecured.

Categorizing Central and State Government dues for the 2 years preceding liquidation (whether secured by operation of law/contract or unsecured) under clause (e)(i), with any excess government dues falling under clause (f).
Proportionate deduction of liquidator fees from proceeds payable to each class of recipients.
statutory_bars: Prohibition against altering or disrupting the statutory waterfall order through contractual arrangements between recipients of different ranking classes.
Prohibition against making distributions to lower-priority classes before higher-priority classes are fully satisfied or paid in equal proportion.
saving_exceptions: Contractual inter-creditor arrangements between creditors belonging to the same equal-ranking class (e.g., inter-creditor subordination among secured creditors) are valid and shall not be disregarded.

section_title: Dissolution of corporate debtor
statutory_summary: Mandates the complete liquidation and dissolution of the corporate debtor upon application by the liquidator within 180 days (extendable by 90 days) or upon CoC decision, while preserving the continuation of pending avoidance, fraudulent trading, and distribution-related legal proceedings.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the corporate debtor's assets have been completely liquidated or a valid CoC dissolution decision was taken under Section 33(2), whether the dissolution application was filed within statutory time limits, and whether appropriate CoC arrangements exist to pursue pending avoidance and litigation proceedings post-dissolution.

applicant_eligibility: Liquidator completing asset liquidation and filing for dissolution under sub-section (1).
Committee of Creditors deciding to dissolve the corporate debtor under Section 33(2).
mandatory_prerequisites: Application by the liquidator to the Adjudicating Authority for dissolution within 180 days from the liquidation commencement date.
CoC determination regarding the manner of pursuing and distributing proceeds from pending avoidance, fraudulent/wrongful trading, or Section 47 proceedings under sub-section (1A).
CoC arrangements for pursuing pending suits or legal proceedings relating to Section 53 distributions under sub-section (1B).
Forwarding a copy of the dissolution order to the corporate registration authority (ROC) within seven days of the order.
Adjudicating Authority passing the dissolution order within thirty days of application/intimation, recording written reasons if delayed.
statutory_bars: Liquidator failing to apply for dissolution within the 180-day window without obtaining an explicit time extension from the Adjudicating Authority.
saving_exceptions: The Adjudicating Authority may extend the 180-day dissolution application period by up to ninety days upon application showing sufficient cause.
Passing of a dissolution order shall not affect or abate the continuation of pending avoidance/fraudulent trading proceedings (sub-section 1A) or Section 53 distribution suits (sub-section 1B).
If assets remain upon a Section 33(2) CoC dissolution order, proceeds are disposed of to pay CIRP costs and any surplus is credited to the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Fund under Section 224.

section_title: Corporate debtors eligible for pre-packaged insolvency resolution process
statutory_summary: Establishes the eligibility criteria and mandatory pre-filing requirements for micro, small, or medium enterprise (MSME) corporate debtors to initiate a pre-packaged insolvency resolution process (PPIRP), requiring specific corporate, director, and financial creditor approvals along with a base resolution plan.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the corporate debtor qualifies as an MSME under the MSMED Act, 2006, meets all statutory non-disqualification conditions under Section 54A(2), and has secured the mandatory majority director declarations, 3/4th partner or special member resolutions, 51% unrelated financial creditor approvals, and provided a compliant base resolution plan.

applicant_eligibility: Corporate debtor classified as a micro, small, or medium enterprise under Section 7(1) of the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006.
Corporate debtor that has committed a default meeting the threshold specified under Section 4.
mandatory_prerequisites: Approval of the proposed Resolution Professional by unrelated financial creditors representing not less than fifty-one per cent in value of financial debt.
Declaration by a majority of directors or partners stating filing within a period not exceeding ninety days, absence of intent to defraud, and the name of the proposed RP.
Special resolution passed by members or resolution passed by at least three-fourths of partners approving the filing of an application for initiating PPIRP.
Approval for filing the PPIRP application from unrelated financial creditors representing not less than fifty-one per cent in value of financial debt.
Prior disclosure to financial creditors of the director declaration, member/partner resolution, base resolution plan conforming to Section 54K, and specified documents before seeking filing approval.
statutory_bars: Corporate debtor has undergone a pre-packaged insolvency resolution process or completed CIRP during the three years preceding the initiation date.
Corporate debtor is currently undergoing a corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP).
An order requiring the corporate debtor to be liquidated under Section 33 has been passed.
Corporate debtor is ineligible to submit a resolution plan under Section 29A.
saving_exceptions: Where a corporate debtor does not have any financial creditors who are not related parties, the required proposals and approvals shall be provided by such persons as may be specified by the Board.

section_title: Duties of insolvency professional before initiation of pre-packaged insolvency resolution process
statutory_summary: Outlines the pre-initiation duties of the proposed resolution professional for a pre-packaged insolvency process, including verifying Section 54A eligibility, ensuring base resolution plan compliance, submitting reports to the Board, and treating pre-initiation fees as PPIRP costs upon admission.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the proposed insolvency professional properly evaluated the corporate debtor's compliance with Section 54A eligibility criteria, verified that the base resolution plan conforms to statutory requirements, and filed the mandatory pre-initiation reports with the Board prior to PPIRP application submission.

applicant_eligibility: Insolvency professional proposed to be appointed as resolution professional and approved by financial creditors under Section 54A(2)(e).
mandatory_prerequisites: Commencement of duties upon financial creditor approval under Section 54A(2)(e).
