Preparation of a report confirming that the corporate debtor meets Section 54A eligibility requirements.
Verification and confirmation that the base resolution plan conforms to requirements under Section 54A(4)(c) and Section 54K.
Filing of the compliance report and other specified documents with the Board (IBBI).
Inclusion of pre-initiation IP fees in pre-packaged insolvency resolution process costs upon admission of the application.
statutory_bars: Cessation of pre-initiation duties if the corporate debtor fails to file the PPIRP application within the timeline declared under Section 54A(2)(f).
Cessation of pre-initiation duties upon admission or rejection of the PPIRP application by the Adjudicating Authority.

section_title: Application to initiate pre-packaged insolvency resolution process
statutory_summary: Governs the filing and judicial admission of an application by a corporate applicant to initiate a pre-packaged insolvency resolution process (PPIRP), establishing a 14-day adjudication window and 7-day defect rectification mechanism.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the application filed by the corporate applicant is complete, meets all prerequisites of Section 54A, and whether any identified defects have been cured within seven days of notice.

applicant_eligibility: Corporate applicant of a corporate debtor that meets the eligibility requirements under Section 54A.
mandatory_prerequisites: Filing the application in the prescribed form, with specified particulars, manner, and fee.
Furnishing all specified information and supporting documentation along with the application.
Compliance with eligibility criteria and pre-filing approvals under Section 54A.
statutory_bars: Application is incomplete and the applicant fails to rectify defects within the statutory notice period.
Failure of the corporate debtor to meet Section 54A prerequisites.
saving_exceptions: Mandatory requirement for the Adjudicating Authority to issue notice giving the applicant seven days to rectify defects before rejecting an incomplete application.

section_title: Time-limit for completion of pre-packaged insolvency resolution process
statutory_summary: Mandates a strict 120-day overall limit for completing the PPIRP, requiring the resolution professional to submit a CoC-approved resolution plan to the Adjudicating Authority within 90 days, or immediately apply for process termination if no plan is approved within that timeframe.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the resolution plan approved by the CoC was submitted by the RP within the mandatory 90-day window from commencement, or whether the RP filed for termination on the day following the 90-day expiry upon non-approval of a plan.

applicant_eligibility: Resolution Professional appointed to conduct the pre-packaged insolvency resolution process.
mandatory_prerequisites: Submission of CoC-approved resolution plan to the Adjudicating Authority under Section 54K within ninety days from the pre-packaged insolvency commencement date.
Completion of the entire pre-packaged insolvency resolution process within one hundred and twenty days from the commencement date.
Mandatory filing of an application for termination of PPIRP by the RP on the day after the expiry of ninety days if no resolution plan is approved by the CoC.
statutory_bars: Submission of a resolution plan to the Adjudicating Authority after the expiry of ninety days from the commencement date without prior statutory relief.
Continuation of PPIRP beyond one hundred and twenty days from the pre-packaged insolvency commencement date.

section_title: Declaration of moratorium and public announcement during pre-packaged insolvency resolution process
statutory_summary: Mandates the Adjudicating Authority to declare a moratorium under Section 14, appoint the Resolution Professional, and cause a public announcement of PPIRP initiation on the pre-packaged insolvency commencement date upon admitting an application under Section 54C.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether an order of admission under Section 54C has been passed triggering the mandatory order of moratorium, appointment of an eligible Resolution Professional (free of pending disciplinary proceedings), and immediate public announcement.

applicant_eligibility: Adjudicating Authority issuing order on the pre-packaged insolvency commencement date along with admission under Section 54C.
mandatory_prerequisites: Order of admission of PPIRP application passed under Section 54C.
Declaration of moratorium under Section 14(1) read with Section 14(3) mutatis mutandis effective until PPIRP completion.
Appointment of the proposed Resolution Professional if no disciplinary proceedings are pending against them.
Immediate public announcement of PPIRP initiation by the appointed Resolution Professional following appointment.
statutory_bars: Appointment of the proposed Resolution Professional named in the application if disciplinary proceedings are pending against them.
saving_exceptions: Where disciplinary proceedings are pending against the proposed Resolution Professional, the Adjudicating Authority shall appoint an RP based on recommendations made by the Board.

section_title: Duties and powers of resolution professional during pre-packaged insolvency resolution process
statutory_summary: Delineates the duties, powers, and governance mechanisms of the Resolution Professional during a Pre-Packaged Insolvency Resolution Process (PPIRP), including claim verification, CoC constitution, monitoring management, filing avoidance applications, accessing financial records, and ensuring statutory cooperation from personnel and financial institutions.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the resolution professional properly exercised statutory powers and fulfilled mandatory duties during PPIRP—including claim confirmation, information memorandum preparation, avoidance transaction investigation, and CoC governance—and whether corporate personnel and financial institutions provided mandatory cooperation.

applicant_eligibility: Resolution Professional appointed under Section 54E to conduct the pre-packaged insolvency resolution process.
mandatory_prerequisites: Confirmation and maintenance of updated list of claims submitted under Section 54G and informing creditors.
Monitoring the management of the affairs of the corporate debtor and informing the Committee of Creditors of any breach by directors or partners.
Constituting the Committee of Creditors, convening, and attending all its meetings.
Preparing the Information Memorandum based on the preliminary information memorandum submitted under Section 54G.
Investigating and filing applications for avoidance transactions under Chapter III or fraudulent/wrongful trading under Chapter VI.
Financial institutions maintaining accounts of the corporate debtor must furnish all requested information to the RP.
Personnel, promoters, management, and service providers must extend all assistance and cooperation under Section 19 principles.
Ratification of pre-CoC RP fees and expenses by the Committee of Creditors.
statutory_bars: Failure or refusal by personnel, promoters, or associated persons to extend cooperation to the Resolution Professional.
Failure of financial institutions to furnish account details and records to the Resolution Professional.

section_title: List of claims and preliminary information memorandum
statutory_summary: Mandates the corporate debtor to submit an updated list of claims and a preliminary information memorandum to the resolution professional within two days of PPIRP commencement, while establishing personal civil liability for promoters, directors, and partners for loss caused by material omissions or misleading disclosures.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the corporate debtor submitted the updated list of claims and preliminary information memorandum within the mandatory two-day timeframe, and whether any material omission or misleading disclosure caused loss or damage to a party, establishing compensation liability against responsible corporate officers.

applicant_eligibility: Resolution Professional receiving disclosures during PPIRP.
Any person sustaining loss or damage as a consequence of material omissions or misleading information in the list of claims or preliminary information memorandum.
mandatory_prerequisites: Submission of an updated list of claims (including details of creditors, security interests, and guarantees) to the resolution professional within two days of pre-packaged insolvency commencement date.
Submission of a preliminary information memorandum containing relevant information for formulating a resolution plan within two days of pre-packaged insolvency commencement date.
Proof of loss or damage sustained due to material omission or misleading information when seeking compensation.
statutory_bars: Corporate debtor's failure to submit required disclosures within two days of pre-packaged insolvency commencement date.
saving_exceptions: Statutory defense against personal compensation liability if the list of claims or preliminary information memorandum was submitted without the knowledge or consent of the promoter, director, partner, or authorizing officer.

section_title: Management of affairs of corporate debtor
statutory_summary: Establishes a debtor-in-possession governance model during PPIRP where the management of the corporate debtor remains vested in its Board of Directors or partners, mandating them to preserve property value and maintain operations as a going concern.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the Board of Directors or partners of the corporate debtor in possession under PPIRP fulfilled their statutory duty to protect and preserve asset value, manage the corporate debtor as a going concern, and comply with prescribed operational restrictions.

applicant_eligibility: Board of Directors or partners of the corporate debtor continuing in possession during the pre-packaged insolvency resolution process.
mandatory_prerequisites: Vesting of management of corporate debtor affairs in the existing Board of Directors or partners during the PPIRP period.
Mandatory duty of management to make every endeavour to protect and preserve the value of corporate debtor property.
Mandatory duty to manage corporate operations as a going concern.
Promoters, members, personnel, and partners exercising statutory/contractual rights and obligations subject to Chapter III-A provisions and prescribed restrictions.
statutory_bars: Failure by management to maintain the corporate debtor as a going concern or willful depletion/diminution of asset value during PPIRP.

section_title: Committee of creditors
statutory_summary: Mandates the Resolution Professional to constitute the Committee of Creditors (CoC) within seven days of the PPIRP commencement date based on confirmed claims, conduct its first meeting within seven days of constitution, and apply Section 21 governance rules mutatis mutandis.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the Resolution Professional constituted the Committee of Creditors within seven days of pre-packaged insolvency commencement based on Section 54F(2)(a) confirmed claims, held the initial meeting within seven days of constitution, and complied with Section 21 requirements as modified for PPIRP.

applicant_eligibility: Resolution Professional appointed under Section 54E responsible for constituting and convening the Committee of Creditors during PPIRP.
mandatory_prerequisites: Constitution of the Committee of Creditors within seven days of the pre-packaged insolvency commencement date based on the list of claims confirmed under Section 54F(2)(a).
Holding the first meeting of the Committee of Creditors within seven days of its constitution.

Compliance with Section 21 provisions (except sub-section 1) mutatis mutandis, with references to resolution professional under sub-sections (9) and (10) construed as references to corporate debtor or resolution professional.
statutory_bars: Failure to constitute the Committee of Creditors or hold its first meeting within the prescribed seven-day timelines.
saving_exceptions: Alteration of Committee of Creditors composition based on an updated list of claims shall not affect or invalidate any past decisions taken by the Committee of Creditors.

section_title: Vesting management of corporate debtor with resolution professional
statutory_summary: Empowers the Adjudicating Authority to displace the debtor-in-possession management during PPIRP and vest management of the corporate debtor with the Resolution Professional upon application backed by a 66% CoC vote and a finding of fraudulent conduct or gross mismanagement.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the Committee of Creditors resolved by a vote of not less than sixty-six per cent of voting share to vest management with the Resolution Professional, and whether the affairs of the corporate debtor during PPIRP were conducted in a fraudulent manner or suffered from gross mismanagement.

applicant_eligibility: Resolution Professional acting pursuant to a resolution passed by the Committee of Creditors with not less than sixty-six per cent of voting share during PPIRP.
mandatory_prerequisites: Resolution passed by the Committee of Creditors by a vote of not less than sixty-six per cent of voting shares resolving to vest management with the Resolution Professional.
Application filed by the Resolution Professional to the Adjudicating Authority in the specified form and manner.
Finding by the Adjudicating Authority that the affairs of the corporate debtor were conducted in a fraudulent manner or subjected to gross mismanagement during PPIRP.
Invocation and application of Sections 14(2), 14(2A), 17, 18(e)-(g), 19, 20, 25(1), 25(2)(a)-(c) & (k), and 28 mutatis mutandis from the date of the order until the end of PPIRP.
statutory_bars: Resolution passed with less than sixty-six per cent of CoC voting shares.
Failure to establish fraudulent conduct or gross mismanagement during the PPIRP period.

section_title: Consideration and approval of resolution plan
statutory_summary: Governs the submission, evaluation, competition, and approval process of resolution plans under PPIRP, requiring base plan submission within two days, direct CoC approval if operational creditors are unimpaired, competitive bidding against third-party resolution applicants if operational creditors are impaired, and a mandatory 66% CoC voting threshold.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the base or competing resolution plan complies with Section 30(1) and (2) mutatis mutandis, whether operational creditor claims were impaired triggering competitive bidding under sub-section (5), whether proper evaluation criteria were applied, and whether the plan secured a 66% CoC approval vote considering feasibility, viability, and Section 53 waterfall priorities.

applicant_eligibility: Corporate debtor submitting the base resolution plan (individually or jointly with any other person).
Prospective resolution applicants fulfilling criteria laid down by the resolution professional with CoC approval.
Resolution professional presenting and submitting resolution plans to the Committee of Creditors and Adjudicating Authority.
mandatory_prerequisites: Corporate debtor must submit the base resolution plan to the resolution professional within two days of the pre-packaged insolvency commencement date.
Resolution plans must conform to Section 30(1) and (2) requirements mutatis mutandis.
Competitive bidding process inviting prospective resolution applicants if the base resolution plan is not approved or impairs operational creditor claims.
Approval of the resolution plan by the Committee of Creditors by a vote of not less than sixty-six per cent of voting share.
Assessment of feasibility and viability, distribution manner, Section 53 priorities, and security interest value by the Committee of Creditors prior to approval.
CoC must require promoters to dilute shareholding/voting/control rights if claims are impaired, or record written reasons prior to approval if no dilution is provided.
statutory_bars: Inability to approve a base resolution plan directly under sub-section (4) if operational creditor claims are impaired (i.e., not providing full payment of confirmed claims).
Failure to achieve sixty-six per cent CoC approval for a selected competing resolution plan, requiring the RP to apply for PPIRP termination.
saving_exceptions: CoC may provide the corporate debtor an opportunity to revise the base resolution plan prior to approval or invitation of third-party plans.
Direct approval of base resolution plan without competitive bidding if operational creditor claims are not impaired.

section_title: Approval of resolution plan
statutory_summary: Governs the judicial approval or rejection of CoC-approved PPIRP resolution plans by the Adjudicating Authority within thirty days, requiring compliance with Section 30(2) and effective implementation, while mandating liquidation if a plan fails to change existing management after a Section 54J order.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the CoC-approved PPIRP resolution plan satisfies Section 30(2) requirements and contains effective implementation provisions, whether defects can be cured upon notice to CoC, and whether a Section 54J management takeover order requires mandatory rejection and liquidation due to failure to change management/control.

applicant_eligibility: Adjudicating Authority evaluating the resolution plan submitted by the Resolution Professional following Committee of Creditors approval under Section 54K.
mandatory_prerequisites: Resolution plan approved by the Committee of Creditors under Section 54K(4) or Section 54K(12).
Judicial satisfaction that the resolution plan complies with all requirements specified under Section 30(2).
Judicial satisfaction that the resolution plan contains adequate provisions for its effective implementation.
Mandatory change of management/control to a person who was not a promoter or in existing management/control where an order under Section 54J(2) had been passed during PPIRP.
statutory_bars: Failure of the resolution plan to meet Section 30(2) requirements or include effective implementation provisions.

Resolution plan retaining existing promoters/management in control where a Section 54J(2) order for fraudulent conduct or gross mismanagement was passed, triggering mandatory rejection, PPIRP termination, and liquidation order under Section 33.
saving_exceptions: Adjudicating Authority may give notice to the Committee of Creditors to rectify any defects in the resolution plan before passing an order rejecting it.

section_title: Appeal against order under section 54L
statutory_summary: Provides that any appeal against an order of the Adjudicating Authority approving a pre-packaged insolvency resolution plan under Section 54L(1) must strictly be made on the statutory grounds laid down under Section 61(3).
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the appeal challenging the order approving the PPIRP resolution plan under Section 54L(1) is strictly founded on one or more of the exhaustive grounds set out under Section 61(3).

applicant_eligibility: Any person aggrieved by an order approving a pre-packaged insolvency resolution plan passed under Section 54L(1).
mandatory_prerequisites: An order of the Adjudicating Authority approving a PPIRP resolution plan under Section 54L(1).
Pleading and establishing specific grounds for appeal strictly matching the grounds specified in Section 61(3).
statutory_bars: Appeals brought on grounds other than those explicitly enumerated under Section 61(3).

section_title: Termination of pre-packaged insolvency resolution process
statutory_summary: Governs the termination of PPIRP due to non-approval of a resolution plan within 90 days, rejection of competing plans, or a 66% CoC vote, requiring the Adjudicating Authority to pass a termination order within 30 days, determine the continuation of avoidance proceedings, allocate costs to the corporate debtor, or order liquidation if Section 54J management takeover was active.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether valid statutory grounds exist for PPIRP termination (expiry of time under Section 54D(3), plan rejection under Section 54K(12), or 66% CoC vote), how pending avoidance/fraudulent trading proceedings shall continue, and whether a prior Section 54J(2) order necessitates a mandatory liquidation order.

applicant_eligibility: Resolution Professional applying upon failure to approve a resolution plan under Section 54D(3) or Section 54K(12).
Resolution Professional intimating the Adjudicating Authority of a Committee of Creditors decision to terminate PPIRP.
mandatory_prerequisites: Application filed by RP under Section 54D(3) (no plan approved in 90 days) or Section 54K(12) proviso (competing plan rejected).
OR intimation by RP of CoC decision to terminate approved by not less than sixty-six per cent of voting shares prior to plan approval.
Adjudicating Authority passing an order within thirty days terminating PPIRP and specifying the continuation manner for Chapter III, Section 66, and Section 67A proceedings.
Corporate debtor bearing the pre-packaged insolvency resolution process costs upon termination.
statutory_bars: CoC termination intimation lacking the required sixty-six per cent voting share approval.
saving_exceptions: Where an order under Section 54J(2) (fraudulent conduct or gross mismanagement) was passed during PPIRP, termination automatically triggers a liquidation order under Section 33 and includes PPIRP costs as part of liquidation costs.

section_title: Initiation of corporate insolvency resolution process
statutory_summary: Empowers the Committee of Creditors during PPIRP to resolve by a 66% vote to terminate PPIRP and convert the proceedings into a regular Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) under Chapter II, while carrying forward PPIRP costs, continuing avoidance proceedings, and calculating look-back periods from the PPIRP commencement date.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the Committee of Creditors passed a valid resolution by not less than sixty-six per cent of voting share to convert PPIRP to CIRP prior to plan approval, whether the corporate debtor is eligible for CIRP under Chapter II, and whether the RP submitted written consent to act as IRP.

applicant_eligibility: Resolution Professional intimating the decision of the Committee of Creditors during PPIRP.
mandatory_prerequisites: Decision of the Committee of Creditors passed by a vote of not less than sixty-six per cent of voting shares before approval of a resolution plan under Section 54K.
Corporate debtor must be eligible for corporate insolvency resolution process under Chapter II.
Intimation of the CoC decision by the Resolution Professional to the Adjudicating Authority.
Submission of written consent by the Resolution Professional to act as Interim Resolution Professional for CIRP.
Passing of order by the Adjudicating Authority within thirty days of intimation terminating PPIRP and initiating CIRP.
Inclusion of PPIRP costs as part of insolvency resolution process costs for CIRP.
Continuation of Chapter III avoidance proceedings and Sections 66 and 67A proceedings during CIRP.

Inclusion of the PPIRP duration when computing relevant look-back periods under Sections 43, 46, and 50, with 'insolvency commencement date' deemed to mean 'pre-packaged insolvency commencement date'.
statutory_bars: CoC conversion resolution passed with less than sixty-six per cent of voting shares.
CoC resolution passed after the approval of a resolution plan under Section 54K.
Ineligibility of the corporate debtor for CIRP under Chapter II.
saving_exceptions: If the Resolution Professional fails to submit written consent to act as IRP, the Adjudicating Authority shall appoint an IRP by referring to the Board under Section 16.

section_title: Application of provisions of Chapters II, III, VI and VII to this Chapter
statutory_summary: Applies specified provisions of Chapters II, III, VI, and VII of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code mutatis mutandis to the pre-packaged insolvency resolution process (PPIRP), subject to defined textual and contextual modifications.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether a statutory provision imported from Chapters II, III, VI, or VII applies to a PPIRP proceeding and has been correctly construed in accordance with the specific adaptation rules and terminology substitutions mandated under Section 54P.

applicant_eligibility: Parties, resolution professionals, creditors, and corporate applicants involved in pre-packaged insolvency resolution proceedings under Chapter III-A.
mandatory_prerequisites: Reading imported provisions (including Sections 24, 25A, 26, 27, 28, 29A, 32A, 43 to 51, and Chapters VI and VII) mutatis mutandis in the context of PPIRP.
Construing references to members of the suspended Board of Directors as members of the active Board of Directors or partners, unless a management takeover order under Section 54J has been passed.
Construing references to Section 25(2)(j) avoidance filings as Section 54F(2)(h) filings by the Resolution Professional.
Construing references to Section 16 (IRP appointment) as Section 54E (RP appointment during PPIRP).
Construing references to 'resolution professional' in Section 28(1) and (4) as 'corporate debtor' in line with debtor-in-possession governance.
Substituting 'pre-packaged insolvency commencement date', 'pre-packaged insolvency resolution process', and 'pre-packaged insolvency resolution process period' for their corresponding CIRP terms.
statutory_bars: Inappropriate application of unadapted CIRP mechanisms that contradict the debtor-in-possession structure or specific statutory modifications under Section 54P.

section_title: Adjudicating authority for corporate persons
statutory_summary: Designates the NCLT having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office as the adjudicating authority for corporate persons and guarantors, consolidates guarantor insolvency/bankruptcy proceedings with the corporate debtor's NCLT bench, grants comprehensive subject-matter jurisdiction over related claims/questions, and excludes the moratorium period from limitation calculations.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the NCLT has territorial jurisdiction based on the registered office location, whether pending insolvency/bankruptcy proceedings of corporate or personal guarantors must be filed in or transferred to the NCLT handling the corporate debtor's CIRP/liquidation, and whether the matter arises out of or in relation to insolvency/liquidation proceedings.

applicant_eligibility: Financial creditors, operational creditors, corporate applicants, resolution professionals, liquidators, or bankruptcy trustees initiating or filing proceedings relating to corporate debtors, corporate guarantors, or personal guarantors.
mandatory_prerequisites: Filing applications before the NCLT bench having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office of the corporate person.
Filing insolvency, liquidation, or bankruptcy proceedings against a corporate guarantor or personal guarantor before the same NCLT bench where CIRP or liquidation of the corporate debtor is pending.
Transferring any pending insolvency, liquidation, or bankruptcy proceedings of guarantors from other courts or tribunals to the NCLT dealing with the corporate debtor.
Exclusion of the moratorium period under Section 14 when calculating the limitation period under the Limitation Act, 1963 for any suit or application by or against the corporate debtor.
statutory_bars: Filing guarantor insolvency or bankruptcy applications in a separate forum or different NCLT bench when CIRP or liquidation against the principal corporate debtor is active.
saving_exceptions: NCLT is vested with all the powers of the Debt Recovery Tribunal (DRT) under Part III for the purpose of guarantor insolvency and bankruptcy proceedings under sub-section (2).

section_title: Appeals and Appellate Authority
statutory_summary: Establishes the right of appeal to the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) for any person aggrieved by an order of the Adjudicating Authority (NCLT), setting a 30-day filing limit (condonable up to 15 days), defining specific grounds for appealing resolution plan approvals, liquidation orders, and PPIRP-to-CIRP conversion orders, and mandating disposal within three months.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the appeal is filed within the 30-day statutory period (or within 15 additional days upon showing sufficient cause), and whether the grounds raised satisfy the specific legal thresholds—such as contravention of law or material irregularity under sub-section (3), or material irregularity/fraud under sub-sections (4) and (5)—for challenging orders under Sections 31, 33, 54L(4), 54N(4), or 54-O(2).

applicant_eligibility: Any person aggrieved by an order of the Adjudicating Authority (NCLT) under Part II of the Code.
mandatory_prerequisites: Filing of the appeal before the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) within thirty days from the date of the Adjudicating Authority's order.
Pleading specific statutory grounds under Section 61(3) when challenging an order approving a resolution plan under Section 31.
Pleading material irregularity or fraud under Section 61(4) when challenging a liquidation order under Section 33, Section 54L(4), or Section 54N(4).
Pleading material irregularity or fraud under Section 61(5) when challenging a CIRP initiation order under Section 54-O(2).
statutory_bars: Appeals filed beyond forty-five days from the date of the order (30 days standard + 15 days maximum condonable period).
Appeals against Section 31 plan approval orders brought on grounds outside those enumerated under Section 61(3).
Appeals against liquidation orders or Section 54-O(2) conversion orders brought without alleging and establishing material irregularity or fraud.
saving_exceptions: Power of NCLAT to condone a delay of up to fifteen days beyond the initial thirty-day limitation period if satisfied that there was sufficient cause for the delay.

section_title: Appeal to Supreme Court
statutory_summary: Establishes a statutory right of appeal to the Supreme Court of India against any order of the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) strictly on a question of law, within forty-five days from receipt of the order (condonable by up to fifteen days upon showing sufficient cause).
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the appeal arises out of an order of NCLAT, presents a valid question of law, and was filed within forty-five days of receipt of the order (or within an additional fifteen days supported by sufficient cause for delay).

applicant_eligibility: Any person aggrieved by an order of the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT).
mandatory_prerequisites: An order passed by the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal under the Code.
Formulation and existence of a question of law arising out of such NCLAT order.
Filing the appeal within forty-five days from the date of receipt of the NCLAT order.
statutory_bars: Appeals filed beyond sixty days from the date of receipt of the order (45 days base limitation + 15 days maximum condonable period).
Appeals brought solely on questions of fact or re-appreciation of evidence without presenting a question of law.
saving_exceptions: Discretionary power of the Supreme Court to allow filing within a further period not exceeding fifteen days if satisfied that the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause from filing within forty-five days.

section_title: Fraudulent or malicious initiation of proceedings
statutory_summary: Empowers the Adjudicating Authority to impose a monetary penalty ranging from one lakh rupees up to one crore rupees on any person who fraudulently or maliciously initiates corporate insolvency, liquidation, voluntary liquidation, or pre-packaged insolvency resolution proceedings for collateral purposes or to defraud any person.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether the initiation of CIRP, liquidation, voluntary liquidation, or PPIRP proceedings was driven by fraudulent, malicious intent, or an intent to defraud rather than a bona fide pursuit of insolvency resolution or liquidation.

applicant_eligibility: Adjudicating Authority acting suo motu or upon an application filed by an aggrieved party, corporate debtor, creditor, or insolvency professional alleging fraudulent or malicious initiation.
mandatory_prerequisites: Filing or initiation of insolvency resolution, liquidation, voluntary liquidation, or pre-packaged insolvency resolution proceedings under the Code.
Evidentiary establishment that the proceedings were initiated fraudulently, with malicious intent, or with intent to defraud any person.
Proof that the purpose of initiation was distinct from the genuine statutory purpose of insolvency resolution or liquidation.
statutory_bars: Failure to establish clear fraudulent or malicious intent (mere dismissal or rejection of an initiation application without evidence of mala fide purpose does not automatically trigger Section 65 penalties).

section_title: Fraudulent or wrongful trading
statutory_summary: Empowers the Adjudicating Authority, upon application by the resolution professional or liquidator, to direct persons knowingly involved in carrying on business with intent to defraud creditors (fraudulent trading) or directors/partners who failed to exercise due diligence despite knowing of imminent insolvency (wrongful trading) to make personal contributions to the corporate debtor's assets.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether business was carried on with intent to defraud creditors or for a fraudulent purpose with knowledge of the parties (sub-section 1), or whether a director or partner knew or ought to have known before the insolvency commencement date that CIRP was unavoidable and failed to exercise reasonable due diligence to minimize creditor losses (sub-section 2).

applicant_eligibility: Resolution Professional during corporate insolvency resolution process or pre-packaged insolvency resolution process.
Liquidator during liquidation process.
mandatory_prerequisites: Application filed exclusively by the resolution professional or liquidator before the Adjudicating Authority.
For fraudulent trading under sub-section (1): Proof of carrying on business with intent to defraud creditors or for a fraudulent purpose, with knowledge of the targeted parties.

For wrongful trading under sub-section (2): Proof that the director or partner knew or ought to have known before the insolvency commencement date that CIRP was unavoidable, and failed to exercise due diligence to minimize potential loss to creditors.
statutory_bars: Bar on filing wrongful trading applications under sub-section (2) in respect of defaults for which initiation of CIRP was suspended under Section 10A.
Applications filed directly by individual creditors, operational creditors, or third parties lacking standing under Section 66.
saving_exceptions: Statutory due diligence defense for directors or partners under sub-section (2) if they exercised such diligence as was reasonably expected of a person carrying out identical functions in relation to the corporate debtor.

section_title: Provisions of this Code to override other laws
statutory_summary: Establishes the supreme overriding effect (non-obstante clause) of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, ensuring that its provisions prevail over any inconsistent provisions contained in any other law for the time being in force or any instrument having effect by virtue of any such law.
core_judicial_inquiry: Whether there exists an inconsistency between a provision of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 and any other law or legal instrument, requiring the provisions of the Code to supersede such conflicting law or instrument.

applicant_eligibility: Any party, resolution professional, liquidator, corporate debtor, or creditor invoking the overriding applicability of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 over conflicting statutes, regulations, or instruments.
mandatory_prerequisites: Demonstrating an operational inconsistency or conflict between a provision of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 and another statute or contractual/statutory instrument.
statutory_bars: Attempting to invoke other statutory remedies or contractual rights that conflict with or subvert the insolvency resolution, moratorium, or liquidation framework under the Code.
